audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Vladimir levels 2, 3 and the first-item row while the matching whys describe Sylas winning all three, and gave only 'Skill' at level 6 where the why says Hijacked Hemoplague kills him. Packet chart reads Skill, Skill, Sylas, Skill, Sylas, Skill, Vladimir on a 49.8% (761 games) even matchup.
audit.why: Level 2 is genuinely even — W is online but Sanguine Pool is not yet a factor. Level 3 and level 6 are Sylas windows because the pool is on a 28s rank-1 cooldown and cannot cover both. Vladimir only owns the two-item row.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 4 and 5 realigned in both layers to Skill, Sylas, Sylas, Skill; ratings rescaled.

audit.why: Four spikes: level 3 full kit, level 6 Hijacked Hemoplague, Riftmaker, and Vladimir's late AP scaling. Order and timing check out against both kits.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three real errors. (a) 'his Crimson Rush passive lets him heal back anything' — Crimson Rush is not an ability; the passive is Crimson Pact and it converts bonus health to AP and back, it does not heal. His sustain is Transfusion (Q). (b) 'E2 chain stuns him' and 'E2 chain lands the stun' — Sylas's E recast pulls him to the target, and there is no stun anywhere in the ability text. (c) Pool quoted as 26 seconds; it is 28/25/22/19/16.
audit.why: A player told E2 stuns will open an all-in expecting lockdown that never arrives, and will misread which cooldown to bait. The passive error also misdirects anti-heal purchasing at the wrong ability.
audit.corrected: Crimson Pact replaced with Transfusion (Q) as the sustain source; the stun claim removed and replaced with the real sequencing (Q slow first, E2 to close); pool stated at 28 seconds at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds appears only as a throwaway clause in the itemization report line; the trading and late-game advice never says anti-heal is what decides the extended fight.
audit.why: Both Transfusion and Hemoplague heal Vladimir, and Hemoplague heals him per champion hit. Without Grievous Wounds the two-item duel is unwinnable regardless of sequencing.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal written into whys[6] and wants.you[1] as the actual prerequisite for committing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tides of Blood being blocked by units was never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's own description says the released blood 'can be blocked by enemy units' — standing behind a minion removes his entire poke pattern, which is the whole levels 4-5 spacing war.

edits.before: This lane is decided by one cooldown: Sanguine Pool. Level 1 you have Q only — chip his step-ups and avoid extended auto-trades since his Crimson Rush passive lets him heal back anything short of a full combo. Level 2 W comes online and turns your autos into a sustain engine, but he has no pool yet so don't over-extend. Level 3 is your first real moment — E1 dash eats his E poke on the shield, then E2 chain lands the stun; follow immediately with Q slow and W burst before he can react. If he pools that first E2, back off, wait 26 seconds, and do it again.
edits.after: This lane is decided by one cooldown: Sanguine Pool, 28 seconds at rank 1. Level 1 you have Q only — chip his step-ups and avoid extended auto-trades, since Transfusion (Q) costs him nothing and heals back anything short of a full combo. Level 2 W comes online and turns your autos into a sustain engine, but he has no pool yet so don't over-extend. Level 3 is your first real moment — E1 eats his Tides of Blood on the shield, Q slow lands first, then E2 pulls you onto him for the W burst before he can react. If he pools it, back off and wait the full 28 out.

edits.before: Full kit: E2 chain stuns him long enough to land Q slow then W burst; your E1 shield absorbs the Transfusion counter-hit and the trade is net positive.
edits.after: Full kit: E2 pulls you onto him but does not stun, so land Q slow first, then W burst; your shield absorbs the Transfusion counter-hit and the trade is net positive.

edits.before: His Q-heal at two items outpaces your W regen; Sanguine Pool eats every E2 commit and resets the fight — play for stolen-R flanks in teamfights, not solo kills.
edits.after: His Q-heal at two items outpaces your W unless you are carrying Grievous Wounds, and pool eats every E2 commit — play for stolen-R flanks in teamfights, not solo kills.

edits.before: Track his pool cooldown and all-in exactly when it expires — that is the only window that reliably sticks
edits.after: Have Grievous Wounds before you commit — Transfusion and Hemoplague both heal straight through your damage otherwise

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a spacing war. He will keep himself just outside E2 range and poke with Transfusion to force small HP leads; weave passive Petricite Burst autos whenever he steps up to last-hit and keep the trades from going too deep. Level 6 flips the equation — your R copies Hemoplague, the nuke he was saving for a teamfight, and suddenly a full E2-Q-W-R rotation kills him outright if pool is down. Force the pool first with a fake step-up, then re-engage with your real combo the instant he reappears. Every time you Hijack is a Hemoplague he cannot use in the next river fight.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a spacing war. He keeps himself outside E2 range and pokes with Transfusion to force small HP leads, but Tides of Blood is blocked by units — hold a minion between you and his poke pattern disappears. Level 6 flips the equation: your R copies Hemoplague, the nuke he was saving for a teamfight, and a full Q-E2-W-R rotation kills him outright if pool is down. Force the pool with a fake step-up, then re-engage the instant he reappears — his own R is a flat 120 seconds, so every Hijack is a Hemoplague he cannot use in the next river fight.

edits.before: Vladimir burns Sanguine Pool on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Vladimir burns Sanguine Pool on nothing — take the twenty-eight-second invitation.

notes: Packet suspectName 'Crimson Rush' confirmed as a fabrication and fixed — the passive is Crimson Pact (bonus-health/AP conversion, no healing) and the sustain being described is actually Transfusion (Q). Also removed two separate claims that Sylas's E2 stuns; it does not, per Riot's text it only pulls him to the target. Hemoplague's 120-second flat cooldown is now stated because it is the reason forcing the fight after a Hijack matters.
